study_id: Hickey et al. - 2023 - Long-Term outcomes in adult patients with congenital heart disease considered for transplantation A

eligibility.Eligibility Rationale: The study involves adult heart transplant candidates/recipients, uses a machine learning decision‑tree model (non‑linear AI), reports survival outcomes, and is a peer‑reviewed observational study published after 2018.

identification_methods.Sponsorship source: National Institutes of Health; American Heart Association; HeartFest
identification_methods.Setting: Single-center tertiary academic hospital (University of Pittsburgh Medical Center)
identification_methods.Comments: Retrospective chart review of adult congenital heart disease patients evaluated for heart or heart+ transplantation.
identification_methods.Institution: University of Pittsburgh Medical Center, Heart and Vascular Institute
identification_methods.Address: John G. Rangos Sr. Research Center, #8122, 4401 Penn Ave, Pittsburgh, PA 15224, USA
identification_methods.Dataset Source: Electronic medical records from University of Pittsburgh Medical Center
identification_methods.Identification Notes: Adults ≥18 years evaluated for heart or heart+ transplantation; 58 patients with complete clinical, hemodynamic, functional and laboratory data included.
identification_methods.Input Variables: Demographics, CHD diagnosis, prior surgeries (sternotomies), NYHA class, cardiopulmonary exercise testing parameters, invasive hemodynamic measurements (PCWP, SVP, EDP), laboratory values.
identification_methods.Missing Data Handling: Patients lacking any of the required data were excluded; no imputation performed.
identification_methods.Methods Notes: Univariate logistic regression and non‑parametric tests performed; significant variables entered into multivariate decision‑tree analysis using JMP software.

population.Inclusion criteria: Adults ≥18 years considered for heart or heart+ transplantation
population.Target Population: Adult congenital heart disease patients considered for transplantation
population.Population Notes: Single-center retrospective chart review of patients evaluated between 2004 and 2014 with follow-up through June 2021
population.Diagnosis: D-transposition of the great arteries with atrial switch (20.7%) most common
population.Diagnosis Overall: D-transposition of the great arteries with atrial switch (20.7%) most common

interventions_outcomes.Intervention Input Data Modality: Clinical variables including hemodynamic measurements, cardiopulmonary exercise testing, laboratory values, imaging data
interventions_outcomes.Feature Selection Method: Univariate analysis followed by multivariate decision‑tree selection
interventions_outcomes.Temporal Handling: Static baseline data at time of transplant evaluation
interventions_outcomes.Interventions Notes: Retrospective chart review of 58 adult congenital heart disease patients evaluated for heart or multi‑organ transplantation; decision‑tree analysis used to identify predictors of survival
interventions_outcomes.Outcomes Notes: Survival outcomes reported for transplanted, waitlisted, deferred and declined groups
interventions_outcomes.Result data Notes: Focus on invasive hemodynamic parameters (SVP, PCWP) identified by decision‑tree as correlating with 1‑ and 10‑year survival
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome group: All adult congenital heart disease patients considered for transplantation (n=58)
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Reporting: Transplanted patients with SVP < 14 mmHg had 100% survival at 1 year
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Metric Definition: Proportion surviving to 1 year post‑transplant decision
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Notes: Invasive hemodynamic parameters (SVP, PCWP) were the strongest correlates of survival
